name: ijson
input_api: ijson.items(BytesIO(local JSON bytes), '') on the default yajl2_c backend
scope: JSON structure and values from a local binary stream; valid nested object and nested array controls
family: ijson yajl2_c C extension / yajl 2.1.1 (rtobar fork) C parser
family_note: ijson selects yajl2_c by default when its _yajl2 extension imports; the harness fails unless ijson.backend_name is yajl2_c. That extension drives yajl's lexer and parser and builds Python values in C. The build embeds the yajl fork commit pinned as ijson's v3.6.0 submodule, using ijson's IJSON_EMBED_YAJL path; official Linux wheels link the same commit as a bundled shared libyajl. Independent of the Jiter, simplejson and CPython json families in this cell. ijson's pure-Python, yajl (ctypes), yajl2 (ctypes) and yajl2_cffi backends are not tested.

name: ujson
input_api: ujson.loads(local JSON bytes); ujson.loads(decoded str) gives the same exact tree on both controls
scope: JSON structure and values from local bytes; valid nested object and nested array controls, each equal to an exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree
family: UltraJSON C decoder (ujson decode.c) / vendored double-conversion 3.2.0 C++ string-to-double
family_note: ujson.loads runs ujson's own recursive-descent C decoder in decode.c, which builds Python objects directly; numbers with a fraction or exponent go through dconv_wrapper.cc to the vendored Google double-conversion 3.2.0 StringToDoubleConverter. Independent of the CPython json (_json scanner), simplejson, Jiter, orjson/yyjson and yajl families in this cell, and of V8 and Rust JSON parsers elsewhere. Other packages that vendor an UltraJSON-derived decoder (for example pandas.io.json) are separate builds and are not covered by this path.
number_and_key_scope: Not exercised beyond the controls; no malformed or edge-case probes were run. From the pinned decode.c source: duplicate object keys are inserted with PyDict_SetItem, so the last value wins; integers without fraction/exponent use a uint64 fast path and fall back to PyLong_FromString on overflow (arbitrary precision); fraction/exponent numbers become binary64 floats through double-conversion; decode_numeric also accepts the non-RFC tokens NaN, Infinity and -Infinity. The controls contain no duplicate keys (checked with the oracle's object_pairs_hook), only exactly representable floats (1.25 and 2.5e-1) and small integers.
